text.p: These are significant stories in the Nigerian press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Head of State General Sani Abacha says it is time Nigeria developed its own technology to serve local needs.
- Government will not be stampeded into granting an increase in local airfares, in spite of demands by airlines for an increase of over 200 percent.
- United Nations Development Programme has earmarked $14 million for technical development of small and medium enterprises as part of a poverty alleviation programme in Nigeria.

- Nigerian Telecommunications signs 5.0 billion naira contract with Germany's Siemens for repairs to exchanges in Lagos districts of Ikeja and Apapa, destroyed in separate fires. The contract will provide another 50,000 lines in Lagos.
- After one week many banks have failed to comply with a central bank directive ordering them to display interest rates prominently. The directive followed the lifting of a ceiling on rates.

- Shell Petroleum Development Company says it does not recognise the Movement for the Survival of Ogoni People (MOSOP). Shell has been trying to return to production in Ogoniland, having been chased out in 1993 after acts of sabotage by MOSOP.
